questions.stem:
A car moves along a straight horizontal road with constant acceleration $a\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ where $a>0$

The car is modelled as a particle.

At time $t=0$, the car passes point $A$ and is moving with speed $u\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$

In the first three seconds after passing $A$ the car travels $20\,\mathrm{m}$.

In the fourth second after passing $A$ the car travels $10\,\mathrm{m}$.

The speed of the car as it passes point $B$ is $20\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$

Find the time taken for the car to travel from $A$ to $B$.
(8)

parts.text:
A car moves along a straight horizontal road with constant acceleration $a\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ where $a>0$

The car is modelled as a particle.

At time $t=0$, the car passes point $A$ and is moving with speed $u\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$

In the first three seconds after passing $A$ the car travels $20\,\mathrm{m}$.

In the fourth second after passing $A$ the car travels $10\,\mathrm{m}$.

The speed of the car as it passes point $B$ is $20\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$

Find the time taken for the car to travel from $A$ to $B$.
(8)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Use of $s=ut+\frac{1}{2}at^2$. Form equation in $u$ and $a$. N.B. Marks are available if they use two other unknowns, rather than $u$ and $a$.
A1: $20=3u+\frac{9a}{2}$ Correct unsimplified equation
M1: Use of suvat. Form second equation in $u$ and $a$. N.B. Marks are available if they use the same two other unknowns, rather than $u$ and $a$.
A1: $10=(u+3a)+\frac{a}{2}$ or $30=4u+8a$ Correct unsimplified equation
M1: $30=3u+\frac{21a}{2}\Rightarrow 10=6a,\ a=\frac{5}{3}$ Solve for $u$ or $a$. Or for one of their unknowns.
A1: $u=\frac{25}{6}$ $u$ and $a$ both correct or both their unknowns correct. Accept equivalent forms. 1.7, 4.2 or better.
M1: Use of $v=u+at$, $20=\frac{25}{6}+\frac{5}{3}t$ Complete method using suvat to find $t$. Correct unsimplified for their $u$, $a$.
A1: $t=9.5$ (s) cao

questions.stem:
[In this question $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are perpendicular horizontal unit vectors.]

Three forces, $\mathbf{F}_1$, $\mathbf{F}_2$ and $\mathbf{F}_3$, are given by

$\mathbf{F}_1 = (5\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{N}$ $\mathbf{F}_2 = (-3\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{N}$ $\mathbf{F}_3 = (a\mathbf{i}+b\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{N}$

where $a$ and $b$ are constants.

The forces $\mathbf{F}_1$, $\mathbf{F}_2$ and $\mathbf{F}_3$ act on a particle $P$ of mass $4\,\mathrm{kg}$.

Given that $P$ rests in equilibrium on a smooth horizontal surface under the action of these three forces,

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) find the size of the angle between the direction of $\mathbf{F}_3$ and the direction of $-\mathbf{j}$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $(5\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j})+(-3\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j})+\mathbf{F}_3=\mathbf{0}$ oe. Use equilibrium to find $\mathbf{F}_3$. Allow use of column vectors.
A1: $\mathbf{F}_3=-2\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j}$ ($\Rightarrow a=-2, b=-3$) Correct $\mathbf{F}_3$
M1: $\tan\theta=\frac{2}{3}$ For an equation in a relevant angle using their $a$ and $b$
A1: $\theta=33.7°$ 34° or better. 0.588 (0.59) rads

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The force $\mathbf{F}_3$ is now removed and replaced by the force $\mathbf{F}_4$ given by $\mathbf{F}_4 = \lambda(\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{N}$, where $\lambda$ is a positive constant.

When the three forces $\mathbf{F}_1$, $\mathbf{F}_2$ and $\mathbf{F}_4$ act on $P$, the acceleration of $P$ has magnitude $3.25\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$

(b) Find the value of $\lambda$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: Resultant force $=(2+\lambda)\mathbf{i}+(3+3\lambda)\mathbf{j}$ Seen or implied. They must collect the $\mathbf{i}$'s and $\mathbf{j}$'s.
M1: $\mathbf{F}=4\mathbf{a}$ oe, where $\mathbf{F}$ is their resultant, seen or implied (could be implied by $|\mathbf{F}|=13$). Must have attempted to add all 3 forces. N.B. $3.25=\frac{1}{4}[(2+\lambda)\mathbf{i}+(3+3\lambda)\mathbf{j}]$ oe Scores B1M1M0M0A0 but allow recovery.
M1: Finding magnitude of their $\mathbf{a}$ or $\mathbf{F}$: $\sqrt{(2+\lambda)^2/4^2+(3+3\lambda)^2/4^2}$ or $\sqrt{(2+\lambda)^2+(3+3\lambda)^2}$
M1: Use of $|\mathbf{a}|=3.25$ or $|\mathbf{F}|=13$ to form (3 term quadratic in $\lambda$) $=0$ ($10\lambda^2+22\lambda-156=0$)
A1: $\lambda=3$ A0 if they give 2 values.

questions.stem:
Figure 1 shows a large bucket used by a crane on a building site to move materials between the ground and the top of the building. The mass of the bucket is $15\,\mathrm{kg}$.

The bucket is attached to a vertical cable with the bottom of the bucket horizontal. The cable is modelled as light and inextensible.

When the bucket is on the ground, a bag of cement of mass $25\,\mathrm{kg}$ is placed in the bucket.

The bucket with the bag of cement moves vertically upwards with constant acceleration $0.2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. Air resistance is modelled as being negligible.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the tension in the cable.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $T-(15g+25g)=(15+25)\times 0.2$ All terms required. Must be in $T$ only. Condone sign errors.
A1: Correct unsimplified equation in $T$
A1: $T=400$ (N) Must be positive

parts.label: b
parts.text:
At the top of the building, the bag of cement is removed. A box of tools of mass $12\,\mathrm{kg}$ is now placed in the bucket.

Later on the bucket with the box of tools is moving vertically downwards with constant deceleration $0.1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. Air resistance is again modelled as being negligible.

(b) Find the magnitude of the normal reaction between the bucket and the box of tools.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $12g-R=-0.1\times 12$ All terms required. Condone sign errors.
A1: Correct unsimplified equation in $R$ only. Allow $+R$ at this stage
A1: $R=119$ (N) (120) Must be positive

questions.stem:
[In this question $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are perpendicular horizontal unit vectors.]

A particle $P$ is moving with constant acceleration. At 2pm, the velocity of $P$ is $(3\mathbf{i}+5\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$ and at 2.30pm the velocity of $P$ is $(\mathbf{i}+7\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$

At time $T$ hours after 2pm, $P$ is moving in the direction of the vector $(-\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j})$

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $\mathbf{a}=\frac{(\mathbf{i}+7\mathbf{j})-(3\mathbf{i}+5\mathbf{j})}{0.5}$ oe. Use of $\mathbf{a}=\frac{\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}}{t}$. Allow $\mathbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{v}$ reversed. Allow use of column vectors.
A1: $\mathbf{a}=-4\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j}$ Or equivalent
M1: $\Rightarrow \mathbf{v}_P=(3\mathbf{i}+5\mathbf{j})+(-4\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j})t$ For their $\mathbf{a}$
A1ft: $=(3-4t)\mathbf{i}+(5+4t)\mathbf{j}$ Follow their $\mathbf{a}$. Must collect $\mathbf{i}$'s and $\mathbf{j}$'s. This could be implied in subsequent working
M1: $\Rightarrow 5+4T=-2(3-4T)$ Use of correct ratio to form equation in $T$ (allow $t$)
A1: $T=\frac{11}{4}$ oe cao

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Another particle, $Q$, has velocity $\mathbf{v}_Q\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$ at time $t$ hours after 2pm, where

$\mathbf{v}_Q = (-4-2t)\mathbf{i}+(\mu+3t)\mathbf{j}$

and $\mu$ is a constant.

Given that there is an instant when the velocity of $P$ is equal to the velocity of $Q$,

(b) find the value of $\mu$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $\mathbf{v}_P=\mathbf{v}_Q \Rightarrow \begin{pmatrix}3-4t\\5+4t\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}-4-2t\\\mu+3t\end{pmatrix} \Rightarrow 3-4t=-4-2t$ and $5+4t=\mu+3t$. Equate velocities and form two equations in $t$ and $\mu$ i.e. must equate coefficients of $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ oe. Follow their $\mathbf{v}_P$
M1: Solve for $\mu$. Follow their $\mathbf{v}_P$
A1: $\mu=8.5$ oe cao

questions.stem:
A fixed rough plane is inclined at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, where $\tan\theta = \frac{5}{12}$

A particle of mass $6\,\mathrm{kg}$ is projected with speed $5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ from a point $A$ on the plane, up a line of greatest slope of the plane.

The coefficient of friction between the particle and the plane is $\frac{1}{4}$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the magnitude of the frictional force acting on the particle as it moves up the plane.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Resolve perpendicular to the plane. Condone sin/cos confusion
A1: $R=6g\cos\theta$ Correct resolution
A1: $F=\frac{1}{4}R=\frac{18g}{13}=13.6$(N) or $14$(N) 2 sf or 3 sf for decimal answer

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The particle comes to instantaneous rest at the point $B$.

(b) Find the distance $AB$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Equation of motion parallel to the plane. Need all terms and dimensionally correct. Condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion.
A1: $-F-6g\sin\theta=6a$ Correct unsimplified equation in $F$. Allow $-6a$ on RHS
M1: $0=5^2+2\times as$ Complete method using suvat and calculated $a$ ($a\neq g$) to find $s$. This is independent of previous M mark but they must have found a value for $a$.
A1: $0=5^2-2\times\frac{8g}{13}s$ Correct unsimplified equation. Allow $(-s)$
A1: $s=2.07$(m) or $2.1$(m) Must be positive.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
The particle now slides down the plane from $B$. At the instant when the particle passes through the point $C$ on the plane, the speed of the particle is again $5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$

(c) Find the distance $BC$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Equation of motion parallel to the plane. Need all terms and dimensionally correct. Condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion.
A1: $6g\sin\theta-F=6a'$ Correct unsimplified equation in $F$
M1: $5^2=0+2a's$ Complete method using suvat, with $a'\neq a$ and $a'\neq g$ to find $s$
A1: $5^2=0+2\times\frac{2g}{13}\times s$ Correct unsimplified equation
A1: $8.29$(m) or $8.3$(m)

questions.stem:
A non-uniform beam $AB$, of mass $60\,\mathrm{kg}$ and length $8a$ metres, rests in equilibrium in a horizontal position on two vertical supports. One support is at $C$, where $AC=a$ metres and the other support is at $D$, where $DB=2a$ metres, as shown in Figure 2.

The magnitude of the normal reaction between the beam and the support at $D$ is three times the magnitude of the normal reaction between the beam and the support at $C$.

By modelling the beam as a non-uniform rod whose centre of mass is at a distance $x$ metres from $A$,

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) find an expression for $x$ in terms of $a$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
Possible equations:
M1A1: $R+3R(=4R)=60g$ [Vertical resolution] For each equation, M1 for correct no. of terms, dim correct but condone sign errors; A1 for a correct unsimplified equation.
M1A1: $\mathrm{M}(A)$, $60gx=R\times a+3R\times 6a$
Alternatively: $\mathrm{M}(B)$, $60g(8a-x)=R\times 7a+3R\times 2a$; $\mathrm{M}(C)$, $60g(x-a)=3R\times 5a$; $\mathrm{M}(D)$, $60g(6a-x)=R\times 5a$
Consistent omission of $g$ could score full marks. Inconsistent omission of $g$ is an A error. All four of these marks could be scored for consistent use of another unknown length which is clearly defined e.g. on a diagram. N.B. M marks only available if using $R$ and $3R$ oe but allow if wrong way round. For vertical resolution, can score M1A1, even if wrong way round.
S.C. $\mathrm{M}(G)$, $R(x-a)=3R(6a-x)$ scores M2A2, -1 each error
A1: $x=\frac{19a}{4}$ oe Or equivalent
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Two equations required.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
A box of mass $M\,\mathrm{kg}$ is placed on the beam at $E$, where $AE=2a$ metres.

The beam remains in equilibrium in a horizontal position.

The magnitude of the normal reaction between the beam and the support at $C$ is now equal to the magnitude of the normal reaction between the beam and the support at $D$.

By modelling the box as a particle,

(b) find the value of $M$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
Possible equations:
M1A1ft: $(\uparrow)$, $60g+Mg=S+S$ [Two equations in two unknowns ($M$ and $S$) required]
M1A1ft: $\mathrm{M}(A)$, $60gx+Mg\times 2a=S\times a+S\times 6a$
Alternatively: $\mathrm{M}(B)$, $60g(8a-x)+Mg\times 6a=S\times 7a+S\times 2a$; $\mathrm{M}(C)$, $60g(x-a)+Mga=S\times 5a$; $\mathrm{M}(D)$, $60g(6a-x)+Mg\times 4a=S\times 5a$; $\mathrm{M}(G)$, $S(x-a)=S(6a-x)+Mg(x-2a)$
For each equation, M1 for correct no. of terms, dim correct but condone sign errors. A1ft for a correct unsimplified equation, follow their $x$. $x$ must be substituted to earn the A marks. Consistent omission of $g$ could score full marks. Inconsistent omission of $g$ is an A error.
A1: $M=50$ Exact answer only.

Possible equations:
M1A1ft: $(\uparrow)$, $60g+Mg=S+S$ [Two equations in two unknowns ($M$ and $S$) required]
M1A1ft: $\mathrm{M}(A)$, $60gx+Mg\times 2a=S\times a+S\times 6a$
Alternatively: $\mathrm{M}(B)$, $60g(8a-x)+Mg\times 6a=S\times 7a+S\times 2a$; $\mathrm{M}(C)$, $60g(x-a)+Mga=S\times 5a$; $\mathrm{M}(D)$, $60g(6a-x)+Mg\times 4a=S\times 5a$; $\mathrm{M}(G)$, $S(x-a)=S(6a-x)+Mg(x-2a)$
For each equation, M1 for correct no. of terms, dim correct but condone sign errors. A1ft for a correct unsimplified equation, follow their $x$. $x$ must be substituted to earn the A marks. Consistent omission of $g$ could score full marks. Inconsistent omission of $g$ is an A error.
A1: $M=50$ Exact answer only.

questions.stem:
Two trams, tram $A$ and tram $B$, run on parallel straight horizontal tracks. Initially the two trams are at rest in the depot and level with each other.

At time $t=0$, tram $A$ starts to move. Tram $A$ moves with constant acceleration $2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ for 5 seconds and then continues to move along the track at constant speed.

At time $t=20$ seconds, tram $B$ starts from rest and moves in the same direction as tram $A$. Tram $B$ moves with constant acceleration $3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ for 4 seconds and then continues to move along the track at constant speed.

The trams are modelled as particles.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Sketch, on the same axes, a speed-time graph for the motion of tram $A$ and a speed-time graph for the motion of tram $B$, from $t=0$ to the instant when tram $B$ overtakes tram $A$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: Correct shape for sketch for $A$, starting at the origin. B0 if solid vertical line at the end of either.
B1: Correct shape for sketch for $B$, must be correct relative to $A$, crossing it and ending at same time. Must be done on the same axes. Tram $B$ starts later and acceleration greater.
DB1: 5, 20, 24 shown. Dependent on previous two marks

parts.label: b
parts.text:
At the instant when the two trams are moving with the same speed, tram $A$ is $d$ metres in front of tram $B$.

(b) Find the value of $d$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: $t=20+\frac{10}{3}\left(=\frac{70}{3}\right)$
M1: Distance travelled for either vehicle
A1: $\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{10}{3}\times 10$ OR $\frac{1}{2}\times 5\times 10+\frac{55}{3}\times 10$ ; $\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{70}{3}+\frac{70}{3}-5\right)\times 10$
M1: Find second distance and subtract
A1: $d=\frac{625}{3}-\frac{50}{3}=\frac{575}{3}=191\frac{2}{3}$ Accept 192 or better.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find the distance of the trams from the depot at the instant when tram $B$ overtakes tram $A$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Equate distances from $O$ at time $t$ seconds and equate, using correct structure – see examples.
A2: $\left(\frac{t+t-5}{2}\right)\times 10=\left(\frac{t-20+t-24}{2}\right)\times 12$ OR $\left(\frac{1}{2}\times 5\times 10\right)+10(t-5)=\left(\frac{1}{2}\times 4\times 12\right)+12(t-24)$ Correct unsimplified equation, $-1$ each error (up to a maximum of 2)
M1: $t=119.5$ Solve for $t$
A1: Distance $=5\times(6\times 44-30)=1170$ (m) Accept 1200 or better
